note: Expected probe outcome per build. A probe MUST succeed on the unpatched build before the patch that denies it lands: a probe that has never succeeded proves nothing, because it may simply be broken. 'beacon' names a path that must appear in the beacon log when the probe succeeds, since a return value does not prove egress. A patchedOutcome other than 'denied' REQUIRES an executable predicate in test/containment/check-probes.ts; free text is not an assertion.

builds.unpatched: every probe with required=true must report 'succeeded'
builds.patched: every probe with required=true must not succeed AND its denial must be corroborated by the host-side filter denial log, unless patchedOutcome names another outcome, in which case an executable predicate must hold

ai-agent-host-autoapprove-setting.why: a rogue agent host asserts _meta.autoApproveBySetting for a host tool; 0009's invokeTool refusal must hold regardless of what the host claims
ai-agent-host-autoapprove-setting.blocked_on: no runner imports test/containment/rogue-extension/ai-probes.js yet, and the class-(e) oracle is a host-side observation (beacon hits, marker, whether chat became usable) rather than a return value, so it needs harness support that does not exist. Marked not-implemented rather than required: a required probe that cannot run reported a pass and counted as evidence of containment.

ai-agent-host-token-push.why: a rogue REH serves agentHostProxy and advertises api.github.com in protectedResources; the client would resolve the user's auth session and forward the real accessToken. Client->server, so neither the RPC choke point nor the channel guard sees it

as-external-uri.why: can mint a tunnel the broker does not see

auth-get-session.why: must return a sentinel, never a reusable token

clipboard-read.why: the clipboard routinely holds a token the user just copied

command-enumeration.why: returning the full registry tells an attacker which host commands to try

host-fs-read-file-scheme.why: file: reaches a host path outside the tab mount

host-fs-read-userdata.why: vscode-userdata: reaches real user settings, which hold a seeded canary

host-fs-write-file-scheme.why: a host write is a code-execution primitive, but a file: write from a remote window is served by the REH's own provider inside the tab: the 2026-11-04 run returned success while nothing happened on the host, so this is kept as a negative control, not a proof

host-fs-write-userdata.why: vscode-userdata: resolves against the host profile directory, so the write actually crosses the boundary

host-terminal-newlocal.why: creates a terminal on the host even in a remote window

host-terminal-sendsequence.why: types into the active terminal; with newLocal this writes the host marker file Its own marker, not the shared one: several vectors write PWNED, so after a patch the shared marker's absence cannot distinguish this chain being denied from another vector not running. This is the chain 0007/0008 exist to close, so its evidence has to stand alone.

launder-await.why: the taint must survive an await; ambient context would not

launder-captured-service.why: handler uses a constructor-injected command service, escaping capability threading; must be caught by the fail-closed backstop
launder-captured-service.knownResidual: ADR 20261104-tab-command-taint.md records this as the taint's main escape

launder-direct.why: its handler resolves ICommandService from the accessor and executes _files.windowOpen

launder-event.why: the taint must survive event re-entry

launder-manage-extensions.why: installing an extension is arbitrary code execution

launder-open-external.why: passes allowTunneling: true, and is reachable directly from $executeCommand

launder-timer.why: the taint must survive a setTimeout

open-external-silent.why: hands a URI to the host opener, leaving the tab without passing its broker

reh-onexecutecommand-manageextensions.why: installing or listing extensions on the trusted side is host code execution

reh-onexecutecommand-openexternal.why: egress from the trusted side, around the tab's broker

reh-onexecutecommand-windowopen.why: the server names a command and the trusted workbench runs it; windowOpen acts on the host UI

reh-resolve-variables-host-env.why: the pty host names strings the trusted side resolves over the host shell environment, so ${env:X} returns host secrets; needs no live pty

secret-read-cross-tab.why: SecretStorage is keyed {extensionId, key} globally, so tab B reads what tab A wrote

secret-write-own.why: seeds the cross-tab read; after patching this is a rewrite, not a denial

state-claim-tab-manager-read.why: the storage id is an argument, so a tab reads the Tab Manager's globalState (seeded with a canary by the harness) by naming its id

state-claim-tab-manager-write.why: the same id argument lets a tab overwrite the Tab Manager's globalState (its pending routes); the harness reads the profile's state database for where the write landed

secret-claim-tab-manager-write.why: a tab writes a secret under the Tab Manager's id; the harness reads the profile's state database for the key it landed under

provider-completion-host-file.why: the handler opens a model on the caller's URI; file: is the host disk, and word-based completion returns its words

provider-hover-host-file.why: the same model-reference read through registerModelAndPositionCommand

setcontext-core-key.why: setContext writes the window's global context, so a tab can flip a core when-clause (remoteName)

webview-egress.why: webviews render in the local trusted renderer, so their fetches have the host's network position

rehProbes.note: Reachable only from the rogue REH fixture; the extension host cannot call these.

channel-download-host-read.why: DownloadServiceChannel revives both URIs from server-supplied arguments

channel-download-host-write.why: the destination URI is chosen by the server

channel-mcp-call-tool.why: callToolForServer invokes a trusted-side MCP tool, a host process with host credentials, with tab-chosen arguments

harness.why: fault channel, not a probe: records why a REH run could not arm, so an unarmed run is visible as ERROR rather than reading as containment

reh-onexecutecommand-manageextensions.why: managing extensions on the trusted side is a host code-execution primitive

reh-onexecutecommand-openexternal.why: egress from the trusted side, around the tab's broker

reh-onexecutecommand-windowopen.why: the server names a command and the trusted workbench runs it; windowOpen acts on the host UI

reh-resolve-variables-host-env.why: the pty host names strings the trusted side resolves over the host shell environment, so ${env:X} returns host secrets; needs no live pty, unlike onExecuteCommand

rpc-proxy-auth.why: returns the host's configured proxy credentials

rpc-secret-identity-spoof.why: extensionId is an RPC argument, so the caller can name vscode.github-authentication and enumerate its stored secrets
